en: Jātaka:
The Section of Sevens, Chapter on the Hen-Fowl (Kukkuvagga)
2. The Manojaja Jātaka:
"Just as when a bow bends down and its string twangs, [so it was with him]."
"Surely my friend Manojā, the king of beasts, is being slain.
Come now, let us go to the forest edges."
I am departing as I please;
such friends as these do not exist,
for while I live, I have found a true friend."
“One who does not associate with evil people attains ultimate happiness;
behold the one who lies upon his back, pleasing to the mind.”
The instruction for Giriya:
"A mother does not rejoice with a son who is an associate in evil."
“Behold this man, charming,
lying there covered in blood.
“In such a way does a person come to this state.”
And he comes to greater evil:
whoever does not act upon the beneficial words of those who see his true welfare.
“Thus he becomes even worse than before,
who, though excellent, associates with base people; behold the excellence of one who has been associated with base people.”
“The Lord of Deer, who was struck down by the forceful rush of the arrow.
“A man falls low by serving the lowly;
he never declines by serving his equal.”
"The best approach arises quickly;
therefore, one should resort to that which is even more excellent than that.
Thus ends the second Jātaka, the Manoja-jātaka.
